audits.title: Addressing Hand Hygiene Compliance in a Low-Resource Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: a Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Hand hygiene protocols
audits.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, IPGMER & SSKM Hospital, Kolkata (low-resource)

cycle1.result: Of 1227 planned contacts: hand-washing 707 (58.6%), hand rub 442 (36%), missed 78 (6.4%); missed rate 20% during resuscitation.

audits.intervention: Hand rubs placed at each bassinet after departmental review.

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Drying neglected in 83% and recontamination in 77% of hand-washes.
audits.citation: Biswas A, Bhattacharya SD, Singh AK, Saha M. Addressing Hand Hygiene Compliance in a Low-Resource Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: a Quality Improvement Project. J Pediatric Infect Dis Soc. 2019;8(5):408-413. doi:10.1093/jpids/piy076. PMID: 30189013.

audits.title: Audit of hand hygiene at Broadmoor, a high secure psychiatric hospital.
audits.standard: Local hand hygiene policy
audits.setting: 23 wards, Broadmoor high secure psychiatric hospital

cycle1.result: Significant deficits in the supply of hand hygiene equipment on wards; staff survey showed need to increase awareness of policy and timing of hand decontamination.

audits.intervention: Equipment ordered; infection prevention link nurse duties clarified (check/order equipment, reminder sessions); posters for patients; alcohol gel dispensers at nursing stations.

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: not reported
audits.citation: Ahmed K. Audit of hand hygiene at Broadmoor, a high secure psychiatric hospital. J Hosp Infect. 2010;75(2):128-131. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2009.10.030. PMID: 20304525.

audits.title: Replicating changes in hand hygiene in a surgical intensive care unit with remote video auditing and feedback.
audits.standard: not reported
audits.setting: Surgical intensive care unit, North Shore University Hospital, Manhasset

cycle1.result: Hand hygiene compliance 30.42% with remote video auditing without feedback.

audits.intervention: Real-time feedback from remote video auditing

audits.other_findings: Improvement sustained over 48 weeks of maintenance.

audits.title: Video Surveillance Audit of Hand-washing Practices in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: WHO hand hygiene technique with soap and water (steps 2 to 7)
audits.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Pramukhswami Medical College, Karamsad, Gujarat

cycle1.result: Of 1081 video recordings: 403 (37.3%) excellent, 521 (48.2%) acceptable, 157 (14.5%) unacceptable

audits.title: Good to Great: Quality-Improvement Initiative Increases and Sustains Pediatric Health Care Worker Hand Hygiene Compliance.
audits.standard: Hand hygiene protocol compliance ≥95% (level of reliability 2) within 9 months
audits.setting: Two paediatric inpatient units, academic children's hospital, Duke University Medical Center, North Carolina

cycle1.result: Average compliance 87%.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles: raising awareness, timely feedback, empowering patients and families, focused education and interdisciplinary hand hygiene champions.

cycle2.result: Compliance ≥95%, sustained for more than 2 years.

audits.other_findings: Weekly random audits by the infection prevention programme with control charts.
audits.citation: McLean HS, Carriker C, Bordley WC. Good to Great: Quality-Improvement Initiative Increases and Sustains Pediatric Health Care Worker Hand Hygiene Compliance. Hosp Pediatr. 2017;7(4):189-196. doi:10.1542/hpeds.2016-0110. PMID: 28280120.

audits.title: Nursing and medical contribution to Defence Healthcare Engagement: initial experiences of the UK Defence Medical Services.
audits.standard: Best practice and DMS care standards for hand hygiene before and after patient contact and VIP scoring for peripheral cannulas
audits.setting: 1000-bed urban hospital in an unnamed partner nation (UK Defence Medical Services Defence Healthcare Engagement)

cycle1.result: Hand hygiene compliance poor on induction; no cannula surveillance (VIP scoring) in place.

audits.intervention: Intensive education, training, demonstrations and coworking; introduction of peripheral cannula care and VIP scoring.

cycle2.result: Second cycle: hand hygiene compliance 69% and VIP scoring compliance 99%. Final cycle: nurses' hand hygiene 75/98 (77%) vs doctors' 76/200 (38%).

audits.other_findings: Nurses' hand hygiene compliance was significantly higher than doctors' in the final cycle; Quality Improvement Champions and a Hospital Oversight Committee were set up.
audits.citation: Bowley DM, Lamb D, Rumbold P, Hunt P, Kayani J, Sukhera AM. Nursing and medical contribution to Defence Healthcare Engagement: initial experiences of the UK Defence Medical Services. J R Army Med Corps. 2019;165(3):143-146. doi:10.1136/jramc-2017-000875. PMID: 30077975.

audits.title: Testing a novel audit and feedback method for hand hygiene compliance: A multicenter quality improvement study.
audits.standard: Hand hygiene compliance on room entry and exit
audits.setting: 5 acute-care hospitals (17 wards, 5 ICUs), Midwestern United States

cycle1.result: Standard overt audit estimates were about 30% higher than covert secret-shopper estimates (OR 9.83).

audits.intervention: Monthly feedback tool reporting compliance from the covert audit method.

cycle2.result: No significant change in compliance between baseline and feedback phases (OR 0.92; 95% CI 0.84-1.01).

audits.other_findings: Feedback did not change hand hygiene behaviour.
audits.citation: Scherer AM, Reisinger HS, Goto M, Goedken CC, Clore GS, Marra AR, et al.. Testing a novel audit and feedback method for hand hygiene compliance: A multicenter quality improvement study. Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol. 2019;40(1):89-94. doi:10.1017/ice.2018.277. PMID: 30430974.

audits.title: Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Intervention to Achieve Sustained Improvement in Hand Hygiene Reliability in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: Optimal hand hygiene adherence (target not stated)
audits.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit, Boston Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline compliance not given in abstract.

audits.intervention: Leadership support, education, patient-family engagement, increased audit frequency, individual feedback and hand hygiene screens showing adherence data outside rooms.

cycle2.result: All clinical groups achieved hand hygiene compliance >90%, sustained for a year.

audits.other_findings: 6,563 hand hygiene opportunities were recorded over 3 years.

audits.title: Criterion-Based Audit of Hand Hygiene Performance During Caesarean Section at a Referral Hospital in Northern Tanzania: An Uncontrolled Interventional Study.
audits.standard: Criterion-based hand hygiene checklist
audits.setting: Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre, Moshi (referral hospital)

cycle1.result: Long nails 15 (25%); polished nails 11 (18%); hand wash with water 73%; correct glove removal 20 (33%); alcohol rub use 2 (3%); no hand wash after procedure 35 (58%).

audits.intervention: Feedback, discussion of findings, training, visual reminders and distribution of alcohol-based hand rub

cycle2.result: Long nails 3 (5%); polished nails 1 (2%); hand wash with water 100%; correct glove removal 66%; alcohol rub use 21 (35%); no hand wash after procedure 10 (17%).

audits.other_findings: Poor knowledge fell from 7 (39%) to 3 (17%).
audits.citation: Sengoka E, Rasmussen L, Msuya M, Kisigo G, Sørensen BL, Chilongola J, et al.. Criterion-Based Audit of Hand Hygiene Performance During Caesarean Section at a Referral Hospital in Northern Tanzania: An Uncontrolled Interventional Study. cycle1.result: Total hand hygiene compliance 52.3%

audits.title: Improving Hand Hygiene Compliance in a Resource-Limited ICU Using a Low-Cost Multimodal Quality Improvement Intervention.
audits.standard: WHO Five Moments for hand hygiene (unit weekly episode-based audit protocol)
audits.setting: 12-bed mixed medical-surgical ICU

cycle1.result: Composite compliance 63.1%; pure adherence excluding non-applicable moments 54.2%.

audits.intervention: Multimodal intervention: education, point-of-care visual reminders, audit feedback and leadership engagement.

cycle2.result: Composite compliance 82.0%; pure adherence 82.5%.

audits.other_findings: Largest gains before touching the patient (+27.0 pp) and after touching surroundings (+40.0 pp); sustainability beyond one month unknown.
audits.citation: Qazi S, Khan MA, Din AU, Saleem N, Atif E, Mazhar MA. Improving Hand Hygiene Compliance in a Resource-Limited ICU Using a Low-Cost Multimodal Quality Improvement Intervention. Healthcare (Basel). 2026;14(3):363. doi:10.3390/healthcare14030363. PMID: 41682212.

audits.title: Hand Hygiene Compliance at a Canadian provincial cancer centre - the complementary roles of nurse auditor-driven and patient auditor-driven audit processes and impact upon practice in ambulatory cancer care.
audits.standard: Hand hygiene compliance before entering and after exiting examination rooms (nurse audit) and within the room (patient audit)
audits.setting: Ambulatory care clinics, CancerCare Manitoba provincial cancer centre, Winnipeg

cycle1.result: Nurse audit compliance ranged from 84% to 96% (7,213 opportunities); patient audit compliance ranged from 57% to 82% (23,402 opportunities); overall 89.2% vs 73.6%.

audits.intervention: not reported

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Nurse audit rates showed no time trend, while patient audit rates rose over time; patients were reluctant to remind staff to clean hands.
audits.citation: Bow EJ, Bourrier V, Phillips D, Winski G, Williams M, Kostiuk N, et al.. audits.title: Illuminating Hand Hygiene Practice: Strengthening the Foundation to Infection Prevention in the NICU.
audits.standard: Proper hand-washing technique (no glowing areas under glow lotion test)
audits.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, St. Boniface General Hospital, Winnipeg

cycle1.result: 19.7% of participants had no glowing areas after hand washing; 39.6% had more than two missed areas.

audits.intervention: Glow lotion and UV light hand-washing audits with feedback and education over two PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 37% had no glowing areas; 20.7% had more than two missed areas.

audits.other_findings: Some staff still had one glowing area, so ongoing intermittent auditing was recommended.
audits.citation: Chubey R, Fraser D, Ruth C, Yi M. Illuminating Hand Hygiene Practice: Strengthening the Foundation to Infection Prevention in the NICU. Neonatal Netw. 2026;45(4):259-268. doi:10.1891/nn-2026-0015. PMID: 42791024.

audits.title: Infection Prevention Performance among Hospital Staff during Vaginal Birth: Results from a Criterion-Based Audit at a Zonal Referral Hospital in Tanzania.
audits.standard: Criterion-based audit criteria set with staff from national and international guidelines
audits.setting: Labour ward, Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre, zonal referral hospital

cycle1.result: Hand washing after a procedure 46.7%; alcohol-based hand rub before procedure 1.7% and after procedure 0%; knowledge test mean 59.3%.

audits.intervention: Discussion of baseline findings with staff, short training session and preparation of alcohol-based hand rub.

cycle2.result: Hand washing after procedure 80% (RR=1.71); alcohol-based hand rub before procedure 33.3% and after 30%; knowledge test 65.3% (not significant).

audits.other_findings: Knowledge test improvement was not statistically significant.
audits.citation: Rasmussen LV, Sengoka E, Maro E, Kisigo G, Rasch V, Sørensen BL. Infection Prevention Performance among Hospital Staff during Vaginal Birth: Results from a Criterion-Based Audit at a Zonal Referral Hospital in Tanzania. East Afr Health Res J. 2021;5(1):36-43. doi:10.24248/eahrj.v5i1.649. PMID: 34308243.
